title: Prime-to-characteristic specialization invariance for smooth proper morphisms
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth proper morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $S$ (its image is a unit in every local ring). Let $F$ be a locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] [def-constructible-locally-constant] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], regarded also as an abelian sheaf. For every $q\geq0$, every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$, and every geometric point $\bar t$ of the strict henselization $S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the specialization map
$$\operatorname{sp}:(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\longrightarrow(R^qf_*F)_{\bar t}$$
is an isomorphism. Higher direct images are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], stalks those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and specialization is induced by restricting pointed etale neighbourhood germs at $\bar s$ to $\bar t$ through $S_{(\bar s)}\to S$. No relative-dimension or finite-stalk hypothesis is imposed.
